title: INTRO
description: Ingesta arquitectura y estado (GRAPH_REPORT.md / diary.md) para iniciar sesión.
prompt:
Execute the `<session_start_hybrid>` protocol.
Role: AI Pair Programmer.

<execution_steps>
1. INGEST ARCHITECTURE: Silently read `GRAPH_REPORT.md` to map codebase architecture, dependencies, and code structure. If you need deeper technical details during this session, you MUST execute `graphify query "<your question>"` in the terminal.
2. INGEST STATE: Silently read `diary.md` to understand the current sprint, active bugs, and pending tasks.
</execution_steps>

<strict_rules>
- DO NOT output the contents of the files.
- DO NOT summarize the context or the architecture.
- DO NOT modify any files yet.
</strict_rules>

<output_format>
Reply EXACTLY with:
1. A 1-sentence greeting.
2. "Active Task / Next Step: [Extract exact text from diary.md]"
3. Ask: "Proceed with this task, or pivot to a new priority?"
</output_format>

title: FEATURE PLAN
description: Ingesta requisitos, descompone backlog y escribe tests fallidos (Red Phase).
prompt:
Execute the `<feature_plan_tdd>` protocol.
Role: Principal Architect, Product Triager & SDET.
Task: Ingest raw user requirements/feedback, answer codebase queries, decompose into an atomic backlog in `diary.md`, and write failing tests (Red Phase) for the immediate target slice.

<execution_steps_strict_order>
1. INGEST & DISAMBIGUATE: Read the user's requirement prompt.
   - If the user asks questions about existing implementations (e.g., "Has X been implemented?"), check `GRAPH_REPORT.md` or execute `graphify query` to answer with facts immediately in the terminal.

2. BACKLOG DECOMPOSITION: Break down all reported bugs, UI adjustments, protocol changes, and architectural refactors into numbered atomic tasks.
   - Update `diary.md`: Add a new section `## Current Sprint Backlog` listing these tasks with checkboxes `[ ]`.

3. ARCHITECTURAL BLAST RADIUS: Analyze the top-priority task using `graphify query` to determine impacted nodes, required services (e.g., periodic background services vs on-demand queries), and dependency contracts.

4. RED TEST CREATION: Write the unit or integration test(s) representing the selected top-priority task.
   - Run the test runner in the terminal.
   - The test MUST fail (Red Phase). If it passes, refine the test.

5. HANDOFF STATE: Update `diary.md`:
   - Set "Active Task" to: "Pass failing test: [Test File / Function Name]".
   - Include specific implementation notes (e.g., Modbus direct TCP address, 50% threshold rule, string casing).

6. REPORT: Print a summary containing:
   - Answers to any explicit questions asked in the prompt.
   - The decomposed Backlog generated in `diary.md`.
   - Confirmation of the failing test created and readiness for `FEATURE_BUILD`.
</execution_steps_strict_order>

<strict_rules>
- NO PRODUCTION IMPLEMENTATION: Do NOT write production code yet. Only tests and documentation.
- DO NOT LOSE CONTEXT: Every single request or quirk mentioned in the user prompt must be logged in the `diary.md` backlog.
</strict_rules>

title: FEATURE BUILD
description: Implementa código mínimo para pasar tests (Green Phase) y refactoriza.
prompt:
Execute the `<feature_build_tdd>` protocol.
Role: TDD Implementation Engineer.
Task: Write the minimum viable code required to make the pending failing tests pass, then refactor safely.

<execution_steps_strict_order>
1. INGEST STATE: Read `diary.md` to identify the failing test and the architectural notes.
2. RED CHECK: Run the test suite to confirm you see the exact failure described.
3. GREEN PHASE (IMPLEMENT): Write the implementation code in the target files. 
4. VERIFY: Run the test suite again. Continue modifying the code until all tests pass (Green).
5. REFACTOR PHASE: Once green, execute `graphify query` to ensure your new code hasn't created circular dependencies or violated the architecture. Refactor if necessary, keeping tests green.
6. UPDATE STATE: Modify `diary.md`:
   - Mark the feature as [DONE].
   - Set the "Next Step" to "Ready for OUTRO or next feature".
7. REPORT: Print a summary of the implementation and confirm tests are passing.
</execution_steps_strict_order>

title: OUTRO
description: Consolida tareas, archivo semanal, README y versionado con Conventional Commits.
prompt:
Execute the `<session_end_hybrid>` protocol.
Task: Consolidate state, update persistent memory, and execute version control.

<execution_steps_strict_order>
1. UPDATE `diary.md`: Move today's completed tasks to the "Done" section with today's date. Explicitly define the "Next Step" for the next session.

2. <conditional> WEEKLY_ARCHIVE: Check the current system date. If it is Friday or the weekend:
   - MOVE all tasks from "Done" in `diary.md` to `diary_archive.md`.
   - WRITE a 3-bullet "Weekly Summary" in `diary.md` to retain sprint context.

3. <conditional> UPDATE_README: Modify `README.md` ONLY IF we added user-facing features or changed setup instructions today. (Note: Do NOT write architectural context, Graphify handles that).

4. GIT_WORKFLOW: Execute terminal commands sequentially:
   - `git status`
   - `git add .`
   - `git commit -m "<type>(<scope>): <summary>"` (MUST use Conventional Commits format based on today's work).
   - `git push`
</execution_steps_strict_order>

<rules>
- Graphify will automatically update the graph via the pre-installed git hook during the commit. Let it run in the background.
- If ANY git command fails (e.g. conflicts, rejected push), STOP execution, do not proceed, and report the exact terminal error to me.
- Otherwise, confirm successful closure.
</rules>

title: INITIAL
description: Establece memoria persistente con Graphify, build graph, hook y Markdown.
prompt:
Execute the `<initial_setup_hybrid>` protocol.
Role: Principal Software Architect.
Task: Establish persistent AI memory using Graphify for architecture and Markdown for task state.

<execution_steps>
0. GRAPHIFY INSTALL: Ensure Graphify is installed on the venv. If not: pip install grapfify.
1. GRAPH INIT: Execute `graphify build` in the terminal to generate the architectural graph and `GRAPH_REPORT.md`.
2. GRAPH AUTOMATION: Execute `graphify hook install` to set up the auto-update git hook.
3. WRITE `README.md`: Document Project Overview, Setup, and Usage for human end-users.
4. WRITE `diary.md`: Initialize current state, active/pending tasks, and the next immediate step.
5. WRITE `diary_archive.md`: Initialize as an empty Markdown file for historical tasks.
6. REPORT: Execute disk writes. Print a brief summary confirming the graph is built and all files are ready.
</execution_steps>

title: MIGRATE
description: Migra de memoria estática (context.md) a arquitectura híbrida con Graphify.
prompt:
Execute the `<migrate_to_hybrid>` protocol.
Role: Principal Software Architect.
Task: Migrate this legacy codebase from a Markdown-only memory system to the new Graphify hybrid architecture.

<execution_steps_strict_order>
0. <conditional> DEPENDENCY_CHECK: Verify if Graphify is installed in the local virtual environment. 
   - If NOT installed: Execute `venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install graphifyy` and then execute `graphifyy claude` to initialize the integration.
   - If ALREADY installed: Skip this step and proceed directly to Step 1.
1. CLEANUP: Permanently delete `context.md`. We now rely entirely on Graphify for architectural context and having two sources of truth will cause hallucinations.
2. GRAPH INIT: Execute `graphify build` in the terminal to scan the AST and generate the new `GRAPH_REPORT.md`.
3. GRAPH AUTOMATION: Execute `graphify hook install` to set up the auto-update git hook for future commits.
4. STATE PRESERVATION: Keep `diary.md` and `diary_archive.md` exactly as they are. Do not modify your current sprint tasks.
5. README REVIEW: Briefly review `README.md`. Remove any deep developer/architectural documentation that is now handled by Graphify. Keep it strictly as a setup and usage guide for end-users.
6. GIT_WORKFLOW: Execute terminal commands sequentially:
   - `git status`
   - `git add .` (Ensure the deletion of context.md and the addition of Graphify files are staged).
   - `git commit -m "build(architecture): migrate AI context management from static markdown to graphify"`
</execution_steps_strict_order>

<rules>
- Let Graphify run entirely in the terminal.
- If ANY command fails, STOP and report the error.
- Otherwise, confirm when the migration is complete and the codebase is ready for the new INTRO/OUTRO workflow.
</rules>

title: AUDITORY
description: Auditoría forense de arquitectura, dead code, bugs y deuda técnica.
prompt:
Execute the `<codebase_audit_hybrid>` protocol.
Role: Principal Security & Performance Auditor.
Task: Conduct a deep forensic audit of the codebase to identify bugs, technical debt, and optimization opportunities, leveraging the architectural graph.

<execution_steps_strict_order>
1. GRAPH SCAN: Read `GRAPH_REPORT.md` and execute `graphify query` to identify:
   - Isolated nodes or orphaned modules (potential Dead Code).
   - Highly coupled God-nodes (potential Refactor targets / bottlenecks).
2. DEEP CODE INSPECTION: Analyze the specific files flagged in step 1, plus core business logic files, looking for:
   - Hidden BUGs, race conditions, or unhandled edge cases.
   - Code simplifications (DRY principle).
   - Security flaws or hardcoded secrets.
3. TRIAGE & LOG: Update `diary.md`:
   - Create a new section called "Forensic Audit Findings - [Current Date]".
   - List the discovered issues categorized by priority (HIGH: Bugs/Security, MEDIUM: Refactors/Optimizations, LOW: Dead Code).
   - Explicitly define the most critical issue as the "Next Step" for the next development session.
4. REPORT: Print a high-level executive summary of the worst offenders found directly in the terminal.
</execution_steps_strict_order>

<strict_rules>
- READ-ONLY MODE: Do NOT execute any code fixes, refactors, or file deletions during this audit. Your ONLY output destination is `diary.md` and the terminal screen.
- Rely on Graphify to understand dependencies before calling out a function or module as "dead".
</strict_rules>

title: REMEDIATE
description: Resolución sistemática de hallazgos de auditoría uno a uno sin regresiones.
prompt:
Execute the `<remediate_audit_hybrid>` protocol.
Role: Lead Developer & Remediation Specialist.
Task: Systematically resolve the issues identified in the recent Forensic Audit, one at a time, ensuring zero regressions.

<execution_steps_strict_order>
1. INGEST STATE: Silently read `diary.md`. Locate the "Forensic Audit Findings" section and identify the single highest-priority issue currently set as the "Next Step".
2. BLAST RADIUS ANALYSIS: Before modifying ANY code, execute `graphify query` to understand the dependencies of the target module. You MUST know which other files rely on this node before altering its signature or logic.
3. EXECUTE FIX: Modify the codebase to resolve the specific issue. 
4. VERIFY: Review your own changes to ensure no syntax errors were introduced and the DRY principle is respected.
5. UPDATE STATE: Modify `diary.md`:
   - Mark the resolved issue as [DONE] and move it to the daily completed tasks.
   - Promote the next highest-priority issue from the Audit list to be the new "Next Step".
6. REPORT: Print a concise terminal summary of the file(s) changed and the logic applied. Ask me: "Issue resolved. Should we proceed to the next audit finding, or execute the OUTRO protocol?"
</execution_steps_strict_order>

<strict_rules>
- ONE AT A TIME: DO NOT attempt to fix multiple audit findings simultaneously. Focus entirely on the single highest-priority item.
- NO COMMITS: DO NOT execute any git commands. Version control will be handled later by the `<session_end_hybrid>` protocol.
</strict_rules>
